iterations.explanation: Five axes cover session, encryption, payments, location, notifications; values mirror codes; data protection constrains payment integration; no feedback was provided.

clusters.name: Session Management Policy
clusters.description: Variation in how authenticated user sessions are terminated or expired, distinct from protecting stored or transmitted data.

values.label: Immediate logout termination
values.description: A manual logout control immediately invalidates the active user session.

values.label: Fifteen-minute inactivity timeout
values.description: The platform automatically terminates sessions after fifteen minutes without user activity.

clusters.name: Data Protection Architecture
clusters.description: Variation in cryptographic protection for personal and payment data, distinct from session lifecycle and external integration structure.

relations.rationale: Encryption and privacy obligations restrict which payment-provider integration designs can safely handle CityBike user and payment data.

values.label: End-to-end encryption
values.description: Data is encrypted both during transmission and while stored, including registration information.

clusters.name: Payment Integration Strategy
clusters.description: Variation in abstraction, delegation, and interchangeability mechanisms for connecting CityBike with multiple external payment providers.

relations.rationale: Payment processing handles sensitive payment data, so provider integration and data-protection architecture jointly address secure payment operations.

values.label: Adapter-based provider abstraction
values.description: A common payment interface uses adapters to hide provider-specific differences and support multiple external platforms.

values.label: Facade-based payment delegation
values.description: A payment facade exposes simplified operations while delegating processing internally to dedicated payment services.

values.label: Strategy-based provider interchangeability
values.description: Separate payment strategies encapsulate provider behavior, allowing payment methods to be added or exchanged without changing core logic.

clusters.name: Bike Location Query Strategy
clusters.description: Variation in how the platform retrieves and filters geographically nearby bikes for ride discovery, separate from notification delivery.

relations.rationale: Nearby-bike discovery and bike-status notifications jointly support the rider’s real-time availability experience, while addressing different architectural concerns.

values.label: Radius-constrained geospatial search
values.description: Location queries return only bikes within the required user proximity radius, such as 1000 meters.

clusters.name: Real-Time Notification Pattern
clusters.description: Variation in event propagation mechanisms for communicating bike-state and usage-history updates to riders, distinct from location querying.

relations.rationale: Notifications may communicate changes to bikes discovered through proximity search, but event delivery and geospatial filtering remain separate design axes.

values.label: Observer-based status notification
values.description: Bike status changes are propagated to interested users or clients through an Observer-style event mechanism.

values.label: Usage-history availability notification
values.description: The system notifies riders when their trip or usage history becomes available for access.

clusters.name: Real-Time and Scheduled Notification Pattern
clusters.description: Variation in event and notification delivery, including observer propagation, asynchronous updates, usage-history alerts, and scheduled rental reminders.

relations.rationale: Notifications may communicate changes to bikes discovered through proximity search, but event delivery and geospatial filtering remain separate design axes.

values.label: Usage-history availability notification
values.description: The system notifies riders when their trip or usage history becomes available for access.

values.label: Observer-based rental-state notification
values.description: Rental-state changes are pushed to UI or application components through observers, with optional asynchronous scheduling support.

values.label: Scheduled pre-expiry rental notification
values.description: A scheduler tracks rental duration and sends riders notifications before the rental reaches its expiration point.

clusters.name: Operational Observability Strategy
clusters.description: Variation in live operational monitoring, aggregation, and presentation of fleet status and usage analytics for support and management.

relations.rationale: Operational dashboards may subscribe to bike-status events, while dashboard aggregation and event propagation remain distinct architectural concerns.

values.label: Real-time operational dashboard
values.description: A live dashboard aggregates bike-status data and usage analytics to support monitoring, capacity planning, and fleet operations.

values.description: Repositories encapsulate bike-data persistence and provide structured querying of usage statistics.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The session-related codes fit Session Management Policy (immediate logout termination; 15-minute inactivity timeout). The payment-related codes are variations of Payment Integration Strategy, and the specific labels (provider abstraction layer, Adapter, Facade, delegated payment services, Strategy, interchangeability) are all instances of that same axis rather than new dimensions. The location-filtering codes are covered by Bike Location Query Strategy (radius-constrained geospatial search). The data-protection code is covered by Data Protection Architecture (end-to-end encryption, including registration data). The notification codes are covered by Real-Time Notification Pattern (Observer-based status notifications and usage-history availability notifications). No open code introduces a distinct architectural concern beyond the existing orthogonal dimensions for CityBike.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing dimensions. The operational dashboard, aggregated bike status data, aggregated usage analytics, dashboard subscriptions, and monitoring event propagation fit Dimension 6 (Operational Observability Strategy), with the observer/asynchronous delivery aspects also aligning with Dimension 5 (Real-Time and Scheduled Notification Pattern). Biometric thumbprint authentication, immediate biometric deletion, verification-code expiration, and the 30-second validity window are covered by Dimension 1 (Access Authentication and Session Policy), which explicitly includes biometric authentication, immediate data deletion, and verification-code validity. Observer-based rental state notifications, asynchronous update scheduling, and real-time bike status updates are covered by Dimension 5. Bike position management, proximity query support, and real-time location tracking are covered by Dimension 4 (Bike Location and Discovery Strategy). Repository pattern for bike data persistence and repository-based usage statistics querying are covered by Dimension 7 (Data Access and Persistence Strategy). Rental duration tracking, pre-expiry notification scheduling, and time-based rental management are covered by Dimension 5 as scheduled rental reminder behavior. No open code introduces a genuinely new architectural concern outside the existing taxonomy's axes.
